optionalSelections.rulesText: If you want each hero to feel unique, you can make it a rule that nobody can pick a Style someone else has. Under this rule, Focused and Fused Heroes can never pick the same Archetype as one another, and Frantic Heroes need to check in with everyone else about what Styles they take. This rule is optional. Use it if you think it'd make the game more fun, or ignore it if you think it wouldn't. High Level play can become difficult while playing within the Niche Protection rule!

forms.name: Blaster Form
forms.descriptionText:
Blaster Form is the multi-targetting master, giving an extra target to every Action you perform. Blaster makes every active type of Style better. Support Styles support more allies, aggro Styles damage more enemies, technical Styles ruin more folks’ days, and so on.

The Blaster Ability allows you to apply your Actions to an additional target for free, every time you use an Action. This extra target is optional, and cannot target anything the Action is already targeting. You can't 'double up.' If you cannot use the extra target, you do not get to use it.

The extra target granted by the Blaster Ability must be within your range, in addition to any targeting limitations provided by the Action itself. So if the Action targets “one enemy within sight”, your extra target must be within sight AND within range. If the Action targets “one adjacent enemy,” but your Stance has a minimum range of 2, you cannot apply the

sourceExplanations.text: Blaster Ability’s extra target, because no enemy is both within range and adjacent to you. Amplify does not have this limitation. Its extra target may be any legal target, from within the Action’s normal targetting options. Actions that target only yourself, like Unbreakable Style's Eyes Open, gain no benefit from Amplify or the Blaster Ability. Valid extra targets include any enemy, ally, or obstacle the Action could have targeted normally, as long as that target is also within your range. If an Action places obstacles, you may use one extra target to place one more of those obstacles. If an Action targets multiple kinds of targets, you decide which one(s) you want to apply your extra target(s) to. You choose what you want your extra target(s) to be as you take the Action. For example, Zombie Style’s Raise The Dead targets one enemy, then places two Copy obstacles adjacent to that enemy. You may use your extra target to either target a second enemy (letting you place two Copies adjacent to each enemy), or you could use your extra target to place a third Copy adjacent to the initial enemy. Frantic Heroes increase the maximum range of the Style they attach to Blaster Form when they make their Stance.

forms.name: Control Form
forms.descriptionText:
Control Form is the counterspell, the negate, the tech cancel of Panic at the Dojo. Control Tokens are a powerful but limited resource that can copy, dodge, or parry anything a foe throws your way. You just need to be within range, and Control’s range boost helps with that.

Control Token: A Unique token primarily granted by Control Form. After an enemy within your range declares and pays for an Action, but before they perform it, you have an opportunity to spend Control Tokens. You may spend 1 Control Token to Copy that Action, 2 Control Tokens to Dodge that Action, or 3 Control Tokens to Parry that Action. Control Tokens may only be used once per turn. Copy: After the Action resolves, you may perform the same Action immediately, as a Reactive Action. For X Values and Gates, use a value of 4. You cannot Copy an Action that is only usable once per turn. Dodge: You or an ally within your range become immune to the Action. That Action will deal no damage, give no tokens, cause no forced movement, and apply no other effects to the one who Dodged it. Parry: The Action is negated and immediately ends. Then, you deal 2 damage to the one who used the Parried Action, and may Move up to 2. Super Moves are not Actions, and cannot be Controlled.

sourceExplanations.text: Frantic Heroes decide whether to increase the maximum range or decrease the minimum range of the Style they attach to Control Form, when they make their Stance. They are not “locked in” to this decision, and may make a different decision when making the same Stance later, even if Control Form is being attached to the same Style.

forms.name: Dance Form
forms.descriptionText: Dance Form excels in repositioning at any moment. You slide across the battlefield as you wish, dragging along enemy and ally alike as you go. A Dancer can never be pinned down, and must always be pursued.

sourceExplanations.text: The first Dance Ability will gain 1 Speed token for each triggered instance. If an Action deals 1 damage to you, then 2 damage to you, you will gain 2 Speed tokens from that Action. The key to a powerful Dancer is in using their Token Actions at just the right moment. How you use your Reactive Actions separates the lesser Dancers from the Olympic contenders.

forms.name: Iron Form
forms.descriptionText: Iron Form is unbreakable, a dominant and incredibly tough Form that can take hit after hit after hit and remain standing after it all. The final Iron Ability can reduce 1 damage from any source of damage. It can reduce an already Reduced Hit. It can reduce damage from Pits or from Traps, or from Burning Tokens. It can even reduce damage from an Unblockable Action that normally prevents Iron tokens! For ordering purposes, Protect goes through the Secure list before going through the Contain list. Once you start resolving the Contain effects, target an enemy within range for them to apply to.

sourceExplanations.text: If you have Armor from multiple sources, then each time any of your Armor triggers, the Iron Ability will give you 1 Iron token. It does not have to be specifically Iron Form’s Armor, any Armor will do.

forms.name: One-Two Form
forms.descriptionText:
One-Two is a highly aggressive skirmisher Form, focused on only two things: Dealing damage, and getting closer so you can deal damage. One-Two Form is a rushdown player’s dream.

One-Two's Abilities are not Actions, so when you use an Ability that triggers off of dealing damage with an Action, One-Two's Abilities do not trigger that Ability again. The extra hits from One-Two's Abilities will remove a Weakness token you hold.This makes One-Two Form excellent for both removing your own Weakness tokens, as well as triggering enemy Armor, to let you get hits in past their defenses.

forms.name: Power Form
forms.descriptionText:
Power Form has a very simple, very effective plan: yell really loud, then hit them really hard. What else do you need?

When you gain an odd number of Speed tokens, the Power Ability keeps the odd token out as a Speed token. So if you should gain 5 Speed tokens, you instead gain 2 Power tokens and 3 Speed tokens.

Normally, you can use 1 Power token to Enhance a Hit. The Power Ability allows you to use up to 3 Power tokens per hit, allowing you to turn even a weak 1 damage hit into a devastating 4 damage blow. Each Power token spent will add “Push 1”, however, so they will be sent flying away!

A full powered Crush is nearly unstoppable. Enemy tokens and Abilities cannot be used in response. On a 9+, they can’t even use Armor! They just get Crushed.

forms.name: Reversal Form
forms.descriptionText: Reversal Form takes its turn slowly, throughout the entire Round. They act when needed, and at no other times. With the right Action at the right time, you can steal an entire turn away. Reversal's Ability triggers when your Armor triggers, no matter how you did it. If you step into a Trap, bam! Gain a 3 . Numbers gained during the End Phase of a turn will not be discarded during that turn, so standing on a Trap will give you a 3 for next turn when it triggers your Armor.

forms.name: Shadow Form
forms.descriptionText:
Shadow Form skulks in the shadows, always moving and never stopping. While Dance Form repositions everyone, Shadow runs away and harries any pursuers instead, leaving obstacles as they go.

Free Movement is granted by spending Speed tokens. When it is your turn, you can use Free Movement as much as you’d like before each Action you perform. Free Movement cannot be used mid-Action - once an Action begins resolving, you must completely resolve the Action before anything else can be done. When it is not your turn, you can only use Free Movement during the Movement Phases. You cannot use Free Movement between Actions when you are not the active character. Free Movement costs 1 Speed token per space. It costs 1 extra Speed token to leave a Pit. If you are playing on a square grid, it costs 1 extra Speed token to move diagonally. Even outside of Free Movement, you can use Speed Tokens to Save Yourself. After you suffer Forced Movement, you may spend 1 Speed token to immediately move one space. If you used this to move out of a Trap, Pit, or Rubble space that you would have landed in, you do not

forms.name: Song Form
forms.descriptionText:
Song Form is the diva of support, improving not just yourself but your entire team. A good beat can pick up any team.

Healing removes damage that has been taken. Healing can never take someone above the maximum hit points of their current health bar. If you heal someone at zero HP, they revive immediately, and may take turns and be attacked by enemies again. When healing does not list a number, it heals equal to the Heal Value, which is set by the Cinematic Weight of the fight.

Choice Actions have you choose one or more options from a list. When performing a Choice Action, each choice is known as an option, and you must perform each option in the order listed.

sourceExplanations.text: Any option you did not pick is ignored, and does not happen. Each choice must be different. When you use Sing Along, for example, you cannot pick “they heal” twice. If you chose “they heal,” the second choice must be one of the other two options. Even though Sing Along and Diss Track force someone else to make the second choice, they still cannot choose the same option you chose.

forms.name: Thorns Form
forms.descriptionText:
Thorns Form is a sinister flower. Its defensive Shields are lined with thorns, damaging any foe that attacks you. But if they ignore you, your Brambles and Blossoms will grow out of control until nothing can stop you. Thorns Form puts its foes into a beautiful lose/lose scenario. One of Thorns Form’s Action Dice is a preset number, and is not rolled. There is no “5” die, you just take a 5 into your Action Pool.

Damage dealt to your Shield by an Ability will not trigger the Thorns Ability. The extra hit from One-Two is not damage from an Action, so you will not deal 1 damage back to them from that hit. If you are Challenged by an Angel, their Angel Ability will deal 1 damage to you. Even if that Challenge came from an Action, the actual damage was dealt by an Ability, so Thorns will not redirect it.

sourceExplanations.text: X Actions include an X listed in their effect, and usually also cost X to perform. You can spend any number in your Action Pool to pay for an X Action, and the X listed in the effect is the same value as the number you used to pay for the Action. For example, if you spend a 4 point Shield to use Brambles, then the effect reads: "Deal 1 damage to up to 4 enemies within Range 1-4, then you gain 2 Power token.” If the Action does not cost X, then the value of X will be defined in the Action’s description. In Brambles’ case, X is the value of the Shield used to pay for Brambles. Brambles will always give you 1 less Power token than the value of the Shield used to pay for it.

forms.name: Vigilance Form
forms.descriptionText:
Vigilance Form is reliability incarnate. You always know exactly what numbers you will have, and you can guarantee being alive to take your turn thanks to its start of turn heal. And if you don’t need the heal, you can get rid of pesky Status tokens that would stop your plans. Vigilance Form’s Action Dice are preset numbers, and are not rolled. There is no “5” die, you just take a 5 into your Action Pool.

Weakness Tokens: Weakness tokens represent the status of lost strength, whether you are drained of energy, blinded, or emotionally compromised. Whenever you deal damage, if you are holding any Weakness tokens, reduce that damage by 2, to a minimum of 0. Then, discard 1 Weakness token.

forms.name: Wild Form
forms.descriptionText:
Wild Form goes hard, harder than your body can handle. You rush in with overwhelming strength, able to pile on pain and use powerful Unique Actions with ease. But if that rush of power doesn’t end the fight, you’re in trouble, as you are left tired, burnt out, weak, and vulnerable. So if you go this hard, you best not miss.

The Bleed Value is set by the Cinematic Weight of the fight. While your current HP is equal to the Bleed Value or less, you are Bleeding. You are still considered to be Bleeding while you are at zero HP. When you take damage that reduces your HP to the Bleed Value or less, you Bleed. You can only Bleed once per Round. If you heal above the Bleed Value and fall below it again during the same Round, you will not re-trigger your Build Ability. If a new Round starts and your HP is below the Bleed Value, “When you Bleed” Abilities will not trigger until you take damage during that Round.

freestyles.descriptionText:
Ego Freestyle gets jealous easily. They think they can power up, right in front of you? Well two can play at that game.

freestyles.name: Mythical Freestyle
freestyles.descriptionText: Mythical Freestyle is the only way to access the Mythical d12 , outside of reaching level 10. Use it wisely.

freestyles.name: Persistant Freestyle
freestyles.descriptionText: Persistent Freestyle never gives up. They bide their time and can take Dice Actions at times no one else could, other than a Demon. The discard protection of the Persistent Ability can let you keep: a 4 and a 1 -or-a 3 and a 2 -or-any single number of 5 or less. .

freestyles.name: Secret Freestyle
freestyles.descriptionText: Secret Freestyle is extremely powerful! But you can only use it once. Once you’ve revealed your secret weapon and spent it, you’re out of luck. Hopefully you pulled it out at just the right time to make a big difference. Oh, and you can’t just start the fight with your secret weapon. It isn’t ready yet, you need to prepare it first.

freestyles.name: Silent Freestyle
freestyles.descriptionText: Silent Freestyle skulks in the shadows, always moving and never stopping. If they catch you, they will kill you, but first: they must catch you.

archetypes.name: Angel
archetypes.descriptionText: Ruinous Guard Archetype Angels are the embodiment of law, purity, and order. Their enemies cannot defy them. Angels will find you, hunt you, and destroy you. Angels are a controlling, defensive Archetype. They specialize in durability and tenacity, and it is a focused tenacity. Angels pick an enemy and they make that enemy’s life real difficult. They are excellent Saboteurs, but can also play a solid Harrier or Attrition game. Angels don't dish out a lot of damage, but they can reliably withstand a ton of it, and they Challenge their enemies to focus on the Angel before they can deal with her friends. The Angel's Ability heals her every turn, so Angels cannot be Taken Out by HP loss while anyone else on her team is still standing. Angels make heavy use of Challenge tokens, using them to control their enemies, and every Style they have gives them a different means of dealing with having a lot of enemies who all want you dead.

sourceExplanations.text: The second half of the Focused Angel Ability does trigger off of the first half. The end result is that at the start of your turn, you Challenge an enemy, deal 2 damage to them, and heal equal to the Heal Value +1. The second half of the Fused Angel Ability does also trigger off of the first half. The end result is that at the start of your turn, you Challenge an enemy, deal 1 damage to them, and heal 2.

archetypes.name: Cavalry
archetypes.descriptionText: Support Mobility Archetype No one keeps up like the Cavalry. Your job is to get in, exactly where you need to be, and keep everyone on their feet. Nobody is there for them like you can be. Cavalry are protectors, heroes, and all around nice people to have on your side of the battlefield. Cavalry provide a wide variety of support abilities for their team, giving Shields to anyone who fights alongside them. The Cavalry can get wherever they need to be and provide just the back up your team needs. This makes them excellent Harriers, with solid Growth potential. Cavalry need to watch their positioning. Many of their Abilities work by being within range of their allies, and being where you need to be can make a huge difference in the flow of battle. Cavalry are all about the team buffs. When you have the Cavalry around, you can expect to get a bunch of small bonuses every turn. When playing as the Cavalry, be sure to keep track of these bonuses for your team, so they can properly take advantage of them.

sourceExplanations.text: The Pull granted by First Aid does not need to be in a totally straight line. You can curve it, so to speak. As long as each space of movement is closer to your target than the previous, it is a valid option. This is especially important because Rubble or Pits will end this movement prematurely, and Pits or Traps will damage you if you rush over them. Avoiding those obstacles is crucial to being a good medic. Shields cannot stack. If you give the 6+ First Aid shield to someone who already held a Shield, they must choose to either take the new Shield, or increase their existing Shield by 1.

archetypes.name: Cyborg
archetypes.descriptionText: Preparation Technical Archetype Cyborgs build power over time. They adapt to the threat in front of them, growing stronger, tougher, or faster, as needed. If you let a Cyborg build up, they will destroy you. Cyborgs is a Growth Archetype, using their constant flow of basic tokens to trigger powerful Unique Actions. They are good at everything, and only weak to being struck down before they can properly prepare. Cyborgs need to pay close attention to their token management. Basic Tokens are their bread and butter, and everything they do relies on keeping a stock of the tokens they need when they need them. With a variety of powerful Token Actions and an Ability that gives you the tokens you need, the Cyborg sets itself up for success. As long as you stay focused, the Cyborg can handle anything in front of them.

sourceExplanations.text: The Cyborg Abilities give you many Basic tokens of each type. The Basic tokens are Iron tokens, Power tokens, and Speed tokens.

Each choice in the Cyborg Abilities is exclusive. If a Focused or Frantic Cyborg chooses to gain 3 Power tokens, they cannot pick Power Tokens for the next two options. They must pick Iron or Speed. And if they choose to gain 2 Iron tokens afterwards, then they are forced to gain 1 Speed token, as it is the only type of Basic token remaining. The XYZ-BURST Archetype Action is the only Action in the game to use multiple different X values. Y and Z function the same as X normally does in other X Actions, but each variable’s value is set separately. While that sounds really complicated, XYZ-BURST’s effect is actually very simple. The healing effect scales with Iron tokens spent, the teleport distance scales with Speed tokens spent, and the damage inflicted scales with Power tokens spent to pay for XYZ-BURST. Easy!

archetypes.name: Demon
archetypes.descriptionText: Ruinous Mobility Archetype Demons are big bullies. They get their strength from making others weak. They drain your strength, toss you aside, and just when you think you've got the upper hand, they sneak in a surprise attack. Demons are an aggressive Archetype, focusing on picking off their enemies one by one. They stay on their feet by keeping their enemies off balance, and limiting their ability to counterattack effectively. They are excellent at Rushdown and solid Harriers, with their ridiculous mobility. Demons need to be wary of their enemy's capabilities, because they are relatively fragile. They rely on their tricks, their Fog and Weakness tokens and teleports, to avoid being punished for their aggressive antics. But what really makes a Demon vicious is their Chaos Tokens, which they can spend to take Actions out of turn. They need to keep track of the best time to use those tokens, because a key interruption can mean the difference between defeat and domination.

sourceExplanations.text: Chaos Token: This Unique Token is only used by the Demon. You may spend a Chaos Token to take a Reactive Action, as if you had spent a 4. Any Action that could be taken by spending a 4 is a valid option for a Chaos Token Action. Chaos Tokens are usable only once per turn.

archetypes.name: Flametongue
archetypes.descriptionText: Aggro Technical Archetype Flametongues want to watch the world burn. They specialize in fire, explosions, and blasts of all sorts, destroying the terrain around them as they fight. They hand out a lot of Burning tokens, which deal more and more damage the more of them your enemies have. Flametongues are vulnerable to foes who can remove tokens easily. The Angel's Purify, the Cyborg's Power Converter, and the Trickster Ability can turn your blistering heat into their own strength. Also, Burning Tokens don't trigger until the end of their turn, and everyone can use Put It Out!, so don't rely solely on Burning Tokens to finish your foes off. The main way a Flametongue defeats their foes is by giving them more to deal with than they can reasonably handle. You give out so many Burning tokens, and lay out so many Traps, and punish them for hitting you, and just make fighting back the last thing they can afford to do.

sourceExplanations.text: The Flametongue Abilities not only give Burning tokens to your enemies, they also accelerate how rapidly they burn. Your enemies don’t just take Burning damage on their own turn, they also take burning damage at the end of YOUR turn.

archetypes.name: Gunkata
archetypes.descriptionText: Aggro Zoning Archetype Gunkata is the ancient combat art of shooting people. Usually with guns. Ideally in the face. Probably a lot. Gunkata is a high-damage Archetype that hits its enemies over and over and over. They embody the idea of death by a thousand cuts, and they do it all from fairly far away, making them phenomenal Harriers. Big downside: your Styles have to deal with a minimum range. You need to be very wary of putting obstacles between you and your targets. Fog completely shuts you down and Walls make life difficult, but Rubble and Traps make it harder for your enemies to punish your ranged pokes. Gunkata has a weapon for every occassion. Play to your strengths and punish their weaknesses, and you'll find that victory is an easy target. Gunkata have 2 Archetype Actions: Grape Shot and Slug Shot.

sourceExplanations.text: “Gunslinger Actions” are labeled as such in their description. Each Gunkata Style has one Gunslinger Action unique to it. Your free Gunslinger Actions from the Gunkata Abilities do not count towards the once per turn Action limit of Reversal Form.

archetypes.name: Phantom
archetypes.descriptionText: Phantoms are strange and unusual. They use their paranormal powers to fight their battles for them. Invisible barriers, telekinesis, teleportation, flight - you have all sorts of strange tricks that are tough for many enemies to handle. Phantom is a flexible Archetype that can adapt to anything. Their main gimmick is granted by their Poltergeist Tokens, which give them the Ability to modify their Actions as they perform them, changing and twisting them to accomplish what they could not before. Phantoms lack power. You need to rely on your team to actually defeat most foes, as the Phantom's Styles don't have any damage dealing Abilities or hard hitting Unique Actions. Phantoms have an answer to every problem, and can control the battlefield as you see fit. The outside of the ring is your friend, and tossing enemies out of bounds is child's play to a Phantom.

sourceExplanations.text: Telekinesis is in the interesting position where you can spend 1 Poltergeist Token to pay for it, then 2 more to enhance it. Since you spent 3 Poltergeist Tokens on a single Action, you get to choose 3 Poltergeist Options that each have an X value of 3. In addition, you will always have spent 1 Poltergeist Token to use Telekinesis, so you will get to pick one Poltergeist Option with an X value of 1, even if you don’t enhance Telekinesis at all.

Poltergeist Token: This Unique Token is used by the Phantom. When you pay the cost of an Action, you may spend Poltergeist Tokens to modify that Action. You can spend up to 2 additional Poltergeist Tokens per Action. If you spend multiple Poltergeist Tokens on an Action, each choice must be different. All modifications made using Poltergeist Tokens are considered to be a part of the Action they modified, and will trigger Abilities as such. X is equal to the number of Poltergeist Tokens spent on this Action. Choose X:  Increase the value of up to X different numbers listed in this Action by 1. This option cannot increase Damage or Choices. (“Choose 2” cannot become “Choose 3”, and “Deal 2 damage” cannot become “Deal 3 damage”)  Increase this Action’s maximum Range by +X.  Start of this Action: you teleport X.  Start of this Action: place Rubble into X spaces within range.  End of this Action: deal 1 damage to X enemies within range.  End of this Action: Push 1 or Pull 1 to X previous targets of this Action. If you spend 2 Poltergeist Tokens on an Action, not only is the Action improved with 2 choices, but X = 2 for each of those choices as well. Do you spend your tokens in bursts for maximum power output, or save some for Telekinesis to disrupt your foes’ plans? Or do you do both, and fully enhance your Telekinesis for maximum Poltergeist power? Reminder: Placing Rubble into a space will remove all other obstacles that were in that space. The final Poltergeist option (Push/Pull 1) can be applied to any targets of the Action. This includes targets given by Poltergeist modifications, such as Rubble placed or enemies damaged.

archetypes.name: Punk
archetypes.descriptionText: Punks are all about tearing down the world. They need to make their mark, stand by their convictions, and rebel against the system. You've got guts, and you're not afraid to show 'em. The more the Punk gets beaten down, the harder they rise up and hit back. The Punk is a tanking Archetype. You want to take hits, because the more you bleed, the stronger you hit back on the rebound. The Punk knows that if you outlast your enemy, you win. The Punk's greatest weakness is biting off more than they can chew. Their Styles and Abilities encourage going aggro, and punishing any enemies who take the bait. But if you aren't careful, you'll wind up hurt. Bait doesn’t live a long life. If you can take the heat, though, nobody hits back like a Punk. Once they give you a reason, nothing will hold you back.

sourceExplanations.text: For example, if your Health Bar has 12 HP when full, and you currently have 7 HP, then you have 5 damage on your current health bar. The Focused and Frantic Punks will add a 5 to their Action Pool, while the Fused Punk will add a 3.

archetypes.name: Teacher
archetypes.descriptionText: Your age only holds you back a little bit. You're strong, but not as strong as you used to be, and your lessons hit harder than your fist nowadays. But if they would listen to their Teacher, those reckless fools can do anything. The Teacher is a support based Archetype that donates Actions to the rest of their team. You don't have much power yourself, although Elder Style lets you draw on the strength you once had. Your real strength is in how much more you let your team accomplish. The Teacher is a force multiplier, improving the output of everyone around them. While force multipliers should be taken out immediately to weaken the team, going down is part of your lesson plan. Once the Teacher falls, their Heroic Spirit kicks in to overdrive. The Teacher is patient, observant, and steady. They know a wide variety of interesting techniques from all sorts of powerful combat styles, and will share those techniques with allies who can stand as their equal.

sourceExplanations.text: The Teacher Abilities will still give you Mentor Tokens while you are Taken Out. A Teacher who has been struck down is more powerful than you can possible imagine. You can use Remember Your Training during your own turn, to perform one Unique Action you know for free. Remember Your Training doesn’t allow the active character to bypass Action limitations. For example, Extreme Violence is only usable once per turn. If you use Remember Your Training on an ally who has already used Extreme Violence this turn, they cannot choose Extreme Violence as their free Action. Mentor Token: This Unique token is only used by the Teacher. Mentor Tokens have the passive effect to improve your Heroic Spirit, letting you mentor your allies and improve their skills. Mentor Tokens may also be used to pay for Remember Your Training. Mentor Token Effect: If you are holding any Mentor Tokens, then when you give your Heroic Spirit, increase one of those numbers by 2. Then, repeat this for each Mentor Token you hold.

archetypes.name: Trickster
archetypes.descriptionText: Everyone loves a good trick, unless the trick was played on them. Tricksters revel in confusion, changing the rules as they go. As long as you can stay one step ahead, nobody can handle you. Tricksters are the Iron token masters, converting your ally’s Status tokens and your enemy’s buffs into more and more Iron. Once you’ve had a little time to build up, you can unleash an endless wave of Token Actions to interrupt your foes and reshape the battlefield. Tricksters are extremely powerful when they have everything they need, but they rely on a lot of things to keep their tricks rolling. You need to build up a pile of tokens to spend on your various Unique Actions, and Trickster Abilities take their sweet time building those up for you. More than any other Archetype, Tricksters need careful planning so you don't run out of tricks right when you need them most. Tricksters are hard to pin down, hard to fight reliably, and hard to deal with. You may not deal the most damage, but you'll give your enemies hell trying to keep up with everything you've got going on. Nothing is easy when you're fighting a Trickster.

sourceExplanations.text: Bag of Tricks has 5 alternative costs. For each you pay, you choose one additional option from the list, to a maximum of all 5 choices if you pay with a 2+ and 1 HP, a 3+, 2 Iron tokens, 3 Speed tokens, and 3 HP. The target of the fourth option of Bag of Tricks decides which token they want to discard. Swapping Spaces is not reduced by Fatigue tokens, and doesn’t discard any Fatigue Tokens either.

archetypes.name: Underdog
archetypes.descriptionText: Desperation Preparation Archetype You're just a regular kid, and you're in way over your head. Or you would be, if being an ordinary underdog didn't make you the most dangerous person in the room at all times. The harder they hit you down, the more they underestimate you, the stronger you rise back up. Underdogs rely on a bit of luck and a lot of tenacity. They’re hard to keep down, and things just keep working out for them somehow. Even when it doesn’t look like it, as they bumble into traps or slip and fall away from their enemies, every mistake is their good luck in disguise.

sourceExplanations.text: Just What I Needed essentially lets you convert any 4 basic tokens into one specific type, right at the moment you need it most. You can run away as if you had Speed, deal damage as if you had Power, or block a big hit as if you had Iron.

The unusual wording of the second half of the Underdog Abilities is that way so end of turn damage from Traps and Burning Tokens will count towards gaining Luck. End of Turn effects happen before those trigger, so it has to be a “start of turn” trigger to count that damage. Luck Tokens are a Unique Token used only by the Underdog. They protect you in unforeseen ways, allowing you to evade danger and keep up with the fight even in the worst situations. Once per turn, after any Action fully resolves, you may spend 1 Luck Token to Teleport 3 and Heal 1. 1 Luck Token may also be used to pay for (part of) any Token Action, in place of up to 3 Basic Tokens, 3 HP, or 3 Shield. This can be used as often as you have Luck Tokens and costs to reduce.

archetypes.name: Wardancer
archetypes.descriptionText: You have mastered the art of combat. And to you, art is exactly what it is: temporary, ever-changing, always improving, never perfect. You fight to perform, and you will put on a better show than anybody. The Wardancer is an aggressive Archetype, focused on high damage dealing and mobility. Wardancer Styles are hyper-focused on specific kinds of aggression, giving you exactly the hammer you need to pound down any nail. Mechanically, the Wardancer has the highest numbers. All of their Unique Actions are Tiered Actions, and they get stronger when you spend larger numbers to use them. Their Ability increases their numbers after they roll, but they still favor Forms with large dice to begin with: Control, Dance, Power, Wild, and Zen Forms especially. The Wardancer is a very simple fighter to play. But simple doesn't mean weak, as they are unrivaled in raw power and speed.

sourceExplanations.text: The Wardancer Abilities do not increase your numbers during Heroic Spirit turns, whether you give your dice or receive someone else’s. When you receive Heroic Spirit, it isn’t your turn, so the Ability will not trigger. When you give Heroic Spirit, you will give your numbers away before the Ability would trigger to enhance them.

archetypes.name: Winterblossom
archetypes.descriptionText: Your style is calm, controlled, precise, and icy. A Winterblossom's fighting style revolves around controlling and weakening your enemies, reducing them to a helpless mess that cannot hope to fight back. The Winterblossom is a controlling Archetype that shuts down your foes, similar to the Angel. But while the Angel buffs herself into being untouchable, the Winterblossom weakens her foes into uselessness, before destroying them with a well-timed power blow. The Winterblossom has no problems against other defensive and controlling foes, winning the war of attrition with ease. But aggressive enemies are a problem, as they can dish out damage faster than you can stop it. One-Two Form is especially bad for you, as its users can remove two Weakness tokens per attack. But if you can pile on the Weakness tokens, your opponents will never be able to touch you.

sourceExplanations.text: Focused and Frantic Winterblossoms give out a Weakness token at the start of every turn, not just yours. Each ally's turn, and each enemy's turn, if there are any enemies within your range, then you will give one of them a Weakness token. Fused Winterblossoms do the same, except they do not give out Weakness tokens during enemy turns.

archetypes.name: The Blur
archetypes.descriptionText: The Blur never stands still. An incredibly fast enemy who proves difficult to catch and impossible to escape.

archetypes.name: The Giant
archetypes.descriptionText: The Giant is big and very, very strong. With great strength and extended reach, they are quite dangerous.

archetypes.name: The Immortal
archetypes.descriptionText: The Immortal drains life with every blow. An incredibly durable enemy who just. Won’t. Die.

archetypes.name: The Machine
archetypes.descriptionText: The Machine is perfection. It is built to do a task, and it will succeed without fail.

archetypes.name: The Necromancer
archetypes.descriptionText: The Necromancer leads an army.

archetypes.name: The Swarm
archetypes.descriptionText: The Swarm is an army of one.

archetypes.name: The Tank
archetypes.descriptionText: The Tank is unbreakable.

archetypes.name: The Untouchable
archetypes.descriptionText: The Untouchable dodges with ease.

styles.name: Halcyon Style
styles.descriptionText: Halcyon Style is focused on Iron tokens and support, so it pairs well with defensive and support Forms. Paying for Token Actions does not count as removing tokens for Halcyon's Ability.

styles.name: Judgment Style
styles.descriptionText: Judgment Style is great for singling out one enemy and making it hard for them to do anything. Reminder: Abilities do not work while you are Taken Out, so once you go down, Challenged enemies will no longer lose an Action Die at the start of their turns, and they may remove your Challenge token safely.

styles.name: Shining Style
styles.descriptionText: Shining Style lets you act as a living wall, completely shutting down enemies limited to Range: 1, especially after you Challenge them. Anyone who tries to ignore or remove your Challenge will suffer blinding pain.

styles.name: Singing Style
styles.descriptionText:
Singing Style sings a dour song that weakens all enemies, and has a strong tendency to change the mood frequently.

Mood Shift applies ALL of your “start of turn” effects as its Action. Any Ability that triggers during Phase 2: Start Phase will be triggered again, as Mood Shift’s effect. This includes your current Archetype Ability, your current Form Ability, the Singing Ability, and your Build. As such, this Style pairs well with Archetypes and Forms with good start of turn Abilities, like Angel, Cavalry, Cyborg, Phantom, Punk, Vigilance Form, Wild Form, and especially Song Form.

styles.name: Winged Style
styles.descriptionText: Winged Style is a highly mobile harassment style, able to be anywhere it needs to be to best cause trouble. The Winged Ability triggers on every turn, not just your own, letting you stay out of reach.

styles.name: Charging Style
styles.descriptionText: Charging Style provides team support regardless of your own positioning, so its ideal for getting your team where they need to be. You are your own ally, so the Charging Ability to move at the start of each ally’s turn includes you, on your own turn. When it is your turn, you will get to Move up to 4 spaces and gain temporary Armor. Temporary Armor is used after all other Armor and only triggers once. Once your temporary Armor has triggered, it is lost. Temporary Armor is a binary - you either have it or you do not. You cannot have multiple instances of temporary Armor.

styles.name: Heroic Style
styles.descriptionText: Heroic Style keeps everyone else safe, no matter what. As long as you're in the middle of the squad, they will barely get hurt at all. If multiple allies with Heroic Style are within range of an ally who took damage, only one of them gets to use the Heroic Ability to redirect that damage. They must choose between them who takes half the hit. You are your own ally, so Burning Heart will also give 2 Iron tokens and 2 Power tokens to yourself.

styles.name: Jumping Style
styles.descriptionText: Jumping Style lets you dive onto threats that need to go down quickly, then leap back out of the fray after you’re done. Sometimes the best team support is to take out the problem yourself. Teleportation is a type of movement that ignores all intervening space. “Teleport three spaces” effectively means “directly enter any space within range 1-3.” You do not take fall damage from Pits or gain Fatigue tokens from Rubble you teleport to, but you do trigger Traps.

styles.name: Rallying Style
styles.descriptionText: Rallying Style is healing focused, capable of picking your whole team back up off the ground. You are your own ally who is within your range, so the Rallying Abilities will heal you at the start and end of your own turn, and a 5+ Group Up will affect you as well as any allies pulled into range.

styles.name: Unbreakable Style
styles.descriptionText: Unbreakable Style lets you buff your team by proxy. Any token you hold becomes a token your friends hold. You are your own ally, so the Unbreakable Start Ability will always give you an Iron token, too.

styles.name: Armored Style
styles.descriptionText: Armored Style is tough as nails. With each Iron token you hold negating two damage instead of one, you are very difficult to take down. Spending Iron tokens to use You, Stay or XYZ-BURST will heal you with the Armored Ability. Temporary Armor is used after all other Armor and only triggers once. Once your temporary Armor has triggered, it is lost. Temporary Armor is a binary - you either have it or you do not. You cannot have multiple instances of temporary Armor.

styles.name: Incinerator Style
styles.descriptionText: Incinerator Style is extremely aggressive, getting enemies out of your face and setting them on fire. Incinerator's Ability only gives one Burning token to a Power-boosted hit, no matter how many Power tokens you spend.

styles.name: Machine Style
styles.descriptionText: Machine Style is a well-rounded Style that pairs well with any Form. A 4+ High Efficiency performs all five choices, in the order listed. An 8+ High Efficiency also performs all five, but at twice the value: you heal 2, gain 2 of each Basic Token, and deal 2 damage to an enemy within range.

styles.name: Rocket Style
styles.descriptionText: Rocket Style carries your allies to where they should be, and pushes enemies away from where they want to be. The Rocket Triggered Ability teleports you AFTER the Push is finished, allowing you to stick right next to them.

styles.name: Syphon Style
styles.descriptionText: Syphon Style filters out excess tokens into more Power, letting you turn weakness into strength. A 6+ Power Converter will steal and/or replace every token of a single type held by your target. So if an ally has 3 Weakness tokens, you may turn them into 3 Power tokens.

styles.name: Dark Style
styles.descriptionText: Dark Style lets you set up a lot of Fog to hide in, and punish any enemies who try to use it by handing them Weakness tokens. For Twilight Sorrow, enemies standing adjacent to Fog still count as being in Fog. Twilight Sorrow gives you the same number of Speed tokens as the number of Weakness tokens it hands out. The Dark Ability replaces any obstacle in your space with Fog.

styles.name: Ogre's Style
styles.descriptionText: Ogre's Style relies on Throws to trigger Watch Your Step, and its Ability makes those Throws better and easier to use.

styles.name: Slasher Style
styles.descriptionText: Slasher Style wants to be in the thick of things. You slowly stalk your foes at the end of every turn, slicing into whatever enemy you can get close to. If they run too far away, you can use your Chaos tokens to Suddenly… be back in position. The Slasher Ability deals damage every turn, not just your turn.

styles.name: Vampire Style
styles.descriptionText: Vampire Style drains power with every blow, growing stronger as your enemies grow weaker. There is no better means of winning a game of Attrition than literally stealing HP and damage from your enemies.

styles.name: Zombie Style
styles.descriptionText: Zombie Style is focused on aggressive defense, dealing damage with your throwaway cannon fodder as you throw more and more at them. You will drown the field in a sea of zombies Copies, and anyone trying to stem the flow will suffer harm for doing so.

styles.name: Blazing Style
styles.descriptionText: Blazing Style hands out Burning tokens to anyone who sticks too close to you. Even if they try to escape, Blazing Speed allows you to use your burnt enemies for mid-turn mobility, catching up to keep the Burning tokens building. Once enough Burning Tokens are in play, Ignition is a powerful finisher, burning down an enemy’s HP all at once.

styles.name: Explosion Style
styles.descriptionText: shards of terrain will hurt any enemies standing too close to the chaos. When you place a Pit directly under an enemy, they immediately take 2 Fall damage unless they can Save Themselves. The Explosion Ability only triggers once per Action. If you destroy 3 obstacles adjacent to a single enemy, that enemy only takes 1 damage. Conversely, if you destroy 1 obstacle adjacent to three different enemies, all three of those enemies take 1 damage.

styles.name: Inferno Style
styles.descriptionText: Inferno Style involves setting yourself on fire to discourage enemies from attacking you. That's just smart. Like all Token Actions, Flame Guard can be used as a Reactive Action on anyone’s turn. If you want to use Heat Sink early, you should start combat in Inferno, but don’t take the first turn. Use Flame Guard during others’ turns to build up Iron and Burning tokens, then get rid of those tokens for value with Heat Sink.

styles.name: Phoenix Style
styles.descriptionText: Phoenix Style rises from the ashes, returning you to life from the brink of defeat. Also, its immune to fire, which is a nice bonus. The Phoenix Ability heals you half as much damage as the Burning tokens would have dealt. So if you held 3 Burning tokens, you would heal 2 when they trigger. If you held 9 Burning tokens, you would heal 5.

styles.name: Volcanic Style
styles.descriptionText: Volcanic Style covers the world around you with fire. Traps within your range are scarier than usual, giving Burning tokens to anyone they successfully deal damage.

styles.name: Akimbo Style
styles.descriptionText: Akimbo Style hits the ground running, firing wildly at your foes then disengaging beyond their reach. The Akimbo Abilities are not optional. At the start of your turn, the end of your turn, and after each Action you perform, you must Move.

styles.name: Crosshair Style
styles.descriptionText: Crosshair Style keeps your enemies in your sights, ignoring their defenses and hitting them where it hurts, as long as you can keep them within your narrow range.

styles.name: Fullmetal Style
styles.descriptionText: Fullmetal Style has a toolbox of unique ammo types, granting you exactly the tool you need to handle your current enemies. Toxin ammo to weaken dangerous foes, Tracer ammo to pick out foes in hiding, and Incendiary ammo to pile the damage on when you don’t need the other two types of ammunition.

styles.name: Quickdraw Style
styles.descriptionText: Quickdraw Style lets you do just a little bit more with any Form, making it a universally solid Style. Thanks to Point Blank Shot, you don’t even need to worry about adjacent enemies escaping your range.

styles.name: Ricochet Style
styles.descriptionText: Ricochet Style spreads your damage around rapidly, letting you remove problematic obstacles and soften up many enemies at once. Trick Shot draws line of sight from the obstacle you chose with Trick Shot, instead of drawing from you. After each Gate, you draw line of sight from the enemy you hit with the previous part of Trick Shot, allowing you to shoot around corners. Trick Shot can shoot through Walls and Fog, by using the Wall or Fog in your way as your target. If you choose a Wall or Fog as the targeted obstacle, any enemy within 3 spaces of that Wall or Fog is a legal target, even if you couldn't hit them normally. If you place your Scatter Shot Rubble directly onto an enemy, the first space of their Push 3 can be in any direction. From there, the remaining two spaces must be away from the Rubble. This gives tons of flexibility on where you want to reposition an enemy.

styles.name: Aura Style
styles.descriptionText: You always count as an ally within range of your own Actions, so Aura Manipulation can give yourself a Shield. Aura Style is a shield-based support Style that punishes enemies who try to attack your team. You both crush enemy shields and bolster allied shields with supreme ease. If you pay for Aura Surge with 1 Poltergeist Token, you will get to pick one Poltergeist Option with an X value of 1.

styles.name: Crying Style
styles.descriptionText: Crying Style weakens all of your enemies at once, while also calling out one specific enemy as the focus of your wailing rage.

styles.name: Puppet's Style
styles.descriptionText: Puppet's Style can re-arrange the battlefield however you see fit. The second Puppet Ability will heal yourself, if you moved during your turn.

styles.name: Spirit Style
styles.descriptionText: Spirit Style is a defensive style, letting your move freely while hiding yourself behind a wall of Copies. Your foes will never be able to tell which one is you, when you can swap spaces with a Copy in an instant.

styles.name: Vortex Style
styles.descriptionText: Vortex Style opens portals you can use to your advantage, both for mobility and as defense. Your movement defies all normal rules, and trying to catch you becomes a game of whack-a-mole. The Vortex Ability only counts for movement, not Range. You cannot stand on a Pit and attack any enemy within Range 1-2 of every other Pit. You must move through them first.

styles.name: Brawling Style
styles.descriptionText: Brawling Style can keep up with the most vicious of foes, staying in the fight with pure willpower. The harder they knock you down, the more damage and status you can ignore.

styles.name: Flashy Style
styles.descriptionText: Flashy Style is all about doing more with less. It favors Forms with many dice to add together with the Flashy Ability. So you don’t need to count them: Show Off has 13 options. If you pay for it using a 13, you get to go down the entire list.

styles.name: Knockdown Style
styles.descriptionText: Knockdown Style loves a good fight, and gives it out as good as it gets. Enemies who rely on hitting you multiple times will regret it. If you use Armor or Iron Tokens or Weakness tokens to reduce the damage you take to zero, the Knockdown Ability does not trigger. They need to deal damage to you for you to hit them back.

styles.name: Mad Style
styles.descriptionText: Mad Style pulls a weapon on ‘em. You don’t need to play fair, you need to win. They can die mad about it.

styles.name: Taunting Style
styles.descriptionText: Not Good Enough gives out two less Weakness tokens than the number you spent on it. For example, if you spend a 9 to use Not Good Enough, you give them seven Weakness tokens. Spending a 1 or a 2 will give them zero Weakness tokens. Taunting Style is a big distraction, letting you Challenge your enemies while keeping enough Iron tokens to survive anything.

styles.name: Decoy Style
styles.descriptionText: The Inspired token you gain from the Motivating Ability is the same as the one used for the Teacher Ability. Motivating Style is a support based style, and lets you fill the role of the Cavalry, encouraging you to group up with your team mates.

styles.name: Elder Style
styles.descriptionText:
Elder Style is a strange beast. It pairs well with any Form, but it also pairs with every other Form and Style you have, due to its Ability. For the purposes of Remember Your Training, while you are in Elder Style you have access to the Unique Actions of all of your Stances.

Elder Style likes Forms with good Unique Actions it can use for free. Some of the best are Blaster Form's Amplify, Iron Form's Protect, Power Form's Crush, and Song Form's Sing Along. You do not need to pair Elder Style with these Forms to use these Actions. You just need to have these Forms among your Stances.

styles.name: Mastermind Style
styles.descriptionText:
Mastermind Style directs your allies, deciding what they do for them. You can also time their actions more directly, whispering Diabolical Plans for exactly when they should strike. While Mastermind does have a Range, it does not use it for any Actions under normal conditions. You will only use this Range for passive Abilities, or if Mastermind Style has its Ability Disabled somehow. Diabolical Plan gives Chaos Tokens to your team, since they perform the Actions you pay for. Once you give them the token, they decide when and how they wish to use it. You laid out the plan, but they have to implement it.

Chaos Token: This Unique Token is normally used by the Demon. You may spend a Chaos Token to take a Reactive Action, as if you had spent a 4. Any Action that could be taken by spending a 4 is a valid option for a Chaos Action. The Action granted by a Chaos Token does not count towards the once per turn Action limit of Reversal Form. Chaos Tokens are usable only once per turn.

styles.name: Patient Style
styles.descriptionText: Patient Style knows they are not the star. The stars are the heroes you have taught. Patient Style buys them time, supporting and protecting your pupils until they are ready to win this fight. “Other Actions cannot be used to perform Take Your Time” means that you cannot use Take Your Time through the effect of other Actions, such as Seize The Moment and Remember Your Training.

styles.name: Training Style
styles.descriptionText: Training Token: This Unique Token is only used by Training Style. You can only use Training Tokens while you are the active character. After any Action you perform, if you still have numbers in your Action Pool, you may spend 1 Training token to increase one of those numbers by 2. You may only spend 1 Training token per Action. Training Tokens have a Token Cap of 4, instead of 10.

styles.name: Caged Style
styles.descriptionText: Caged Style traps your enemies until you're ready to let them go.

styles.name: Hidden Style
styles.descriptionText: The Mysterious Ability replaces an obstacle in your space with Fog. You can pay for Ghost Walk with any quantity of each token, as long as you spend a total of 3 tokens. 3 Speed, 2 Speed and 1 Iron, 2 Iron and 1 Speed, and 3 Iron tokens are all legal costs to pay for Ghost Walk. Mysterious Style strikes from hiding, using Fog to be untouchable.

styles.name: Mirrored Style
styles.descriptionText: Illusion Style punishes enemies who try to hurt you without clearing out your Copies. Once you set up, it takes a lot of effort to set you back.

styles.name: Parkour Style
styles.descriptionText: The Hidden Ability lets you stand in Walls. A Wall you are standing in does not block line of sight to you. Hidden Style is a defense oriented Style, but is generically useful with any Form you want to pair it with.

styles.name: Whip Style
styles.descriptionText: The Whip Ability prevents you from Throwing adjacent enemies. Whip Style is a zoning Style, staying out of enemy range and keeping your enemies from getting close.

styles.name: Collateral Style
styles.descriptionText: Collateral Style tears the arena apart. If your enemies were relying on walls and traps to protect themselves, Collateral will put a stop to that.

styles.name: Distracting Style
styles.descriptionText: Distracting Style makes you the perfect distraction. Hard to catch and hard to hit, you can outlast all but the most aggressive assaults. Be sure to Challenge your enemies, so the distraction works!

styles.name: Lucky Style
styles.descriptionText: Lucky Style is basic, but extremely solid, granting you both Armor and an extra Action each turn. It combines well with any Form.

styles.name: Misfortune's Style
styles.descriptionText: Misfortune's Style turns your bad luck around, filling the terrain with Traps while becoming immune to them yourself. Damage that does not come from Actions or Abilities includes: Damage from Traps, from Pits, from Fall Damage, and from Burning Tokens. Karma does not have any range requirements. The target is the active character, regardless of where they are or where you are.

styles.name: Scrambling Style
styles.descriptionText: Scrambling Style keeps moving. If any enemy gets too close, just throw something at their face, or knock over a convenient pile of bricks, and keep running until you can turn the tide.

styles.name: Artistic Style
styles.descriptionText: Artistic Style paints a beautiful picture upon your enemies.

styles.name: Overwhelming Style
styles.descriptionText: Overwhelming Style can break through the mightiest defenses, leaving your enemies reeling from your mere presence. Unblockable means “this defense can’t be used.” So, Armor cannot be used to reduce damage you deal while in Overwhelming Style.

styles.name: Relentless Style
styles.descriptionText: Relentless Style lets you smash your foes across the battlefield, Pushing them away with every strike. Once you have your target, they cannot escape you.

styles.name: Swift Style
styles.descriptionText: Swift Style is fast. Real fast. So fast they can't see it coming.

styles.name: Weightless Style
styles.descriptionText: Weightless Style ignores trouble in a way no other Style can. You have no way of stopping their tricks, so why not just ignore them?

styles.name: Avalanche Style
styles.descriptionText: Avalanche Style is the ultimate defensive combat style, building a wall to hide behind while you continue to strike out at your foes. Your defensive fortifications will never fall! Probably!

styles.name: Crystal Style
styles.descriptionText: Crystal Style creates explosive fragments of glass with everything it does, the shrapnel piercing nearby foes as you go. The Crystal Passive Ability requires the Action to target exactly one enemy, ally, or obstacle. If an Action could have multiple targets (such as Secure or Brambles) but you choose the same target for each, then the Crystal Ability will apply.

styles.name: Frozen Style
styles.descriptionText: Frozen Style makes it difficult to attack you, as anyone doing so has their strength stolen away from them.

styles.name: Heartless Style
styles.descriptionText: Heartless Style punishes defensive strategies, crashing straight through their Shields. Your powerful (but expensive) Unique Actions pierce right through everything else. Unblockable means “this defense can’t be used.” So, Iron Tokens cannot be used to reduce damage dealt by Block This. Paying HP does not trigger Bleeding or any Abilities that trigger on taking or dealing damage. It cannot be reduced by Iron tokens, by Armor, by Shields, or by any defensive Abilities.

styles.name: Pressure Style
styles.descriptionText: Pressure Style is your big finisher. Once your enemies are drowning in Status tokens, Apply Pressure will destroy them.

builds.name: Agile Build
builds.descriptionText: You dodge every blow that comes your way. You see it coming, you see it pass you by, you get away, until you take that one big hit that takes you out.

builds.name: Bumbling Build
builds.descriptionText: You avoid hits by the narrowest margin, right up until the last hit makes you drop. Every hit point before your last one is your luck running out.

builds.name: Mysterious Build
builds.descriptionText: Your actions are mysterious, your movements unpredictable. You hide behind illusions and smoke. But once they see through it all, you’re done for.

builds.name: Overpowering Build
builds.descriptionText: You deflect, blast, punch, or otherwise actively stop everything coming your way. Your strength is unparalleled, but you can’t take that hit that gets through.

builds.name: Scheming Build
builds.descriptionText: You fight dirty, breaking the 'rules' as others expect them. Every hit point is another trick you’ve thrown in their face, until you finally get what’s coming to you.

builds.name: Tough Build
builds.descriptionText: You take hits and keep on going like nothing happened. Damage to you makes you bleed, makes you hurt, makes you suffer, and you don’t care. You can take it. Every fight ends with you covered in blood, and only some of it is yours.

skills.name: Basically Magic
skills.rulesText: You have an ability that's beyond normal, like lycanthropy, telekinesis, fire magic, ghost powers, or something else. When you take this skill, write down what kind of power you have.

effect.text: You have an ability that's beyond normal, like lycanthropy, telekinesis, fire magic, ghost powers, or something else. When you take this skill, write down what kind of power you have.

skills.name: Professional
skills.rulesText: You always look stylish, cool, and in control. People listen when you make demands of them, and you have some lackeys or followers who will do what you say.

effect.text: You always look stylish, cool, and in control. People listen when you make demands of them, and you have some lackeys or followers who will do what you say.

skills.name: Put On A Show
skills.rulesText: You can draw as much attention as you want, whenever you want it, away from anything else, for any reason.

effect.text: You can draw as much attention as you want, whenever you want it, away from anything else, for any reason.

skills.name: Immovable
skills.rulesText: When you plant your feet and stand your ground, nothing can get past you or hurt you, not even vehicles or gunfire.

effect.text: When you plant your feet and stand your ground, nothing can get past you or hurt you, not even vehicles or gunfire.

skills.name: Think Fast
skills.rulesText: You can come up with plans and act on them in an instant. You never lose in games of skill, and you can fast talk anyone into seeing things your way.

effect.text: You can come up with plans and act on them in an instant. You never lose in games of skill, and you can fast talk anyone into seeing things your way.

skills.name: Unstoppable
skills.rulesText: You can smash through any door, wall, or vehicle.

effect.text: You can smash through any door, wall, or vehicle.

skills.name: Perfect Timing
skills.rulesText: You are always in the right place at the right time. You can perfectly catch or stop anything coming directly at you with a single, well-placed motion.

effect.text: You are always in the right place at the right time. You can perfectly catch or stop anything coming directly at you with a single, well-placed motion.

skills.name: Shadow Walker
skills.rulesText: If you don't want to draw attention to yourself, no one will ever notice you sneaking around, even in plain sight.

effect.text: If you don't want to draw attention to yourself, no one will ever notice you sneaking around, even in plain sight.

skills.name: Natural Charisma
skills.rulesText: People naturally like you. Anyone who is not your enemy is your friend, even if you've just met them.

effect.text: People naturally like you. Anyone who is not your enemy is your friend, even if you've just met them.

skills.name: Rose Heart
skills.rulesText: You can redirect others' anger to more productive ends. Your soothing voice and gentle touch can calm rampaging beasts, unruly mobs, and anyone else acting out of hurt or anger.

effect.text: You can redirect others' anger to more productive ends. Your soothing voice and gentle touch can calm rampaging beasts, unruly mobs, and anyone else acting out of hurt or anger.

skills.name: Eyes Wide Open
skills.rulesText: Your senses are unusually strong. You cannot be surprised by anything, and always have a chance to react first.

effect.text: Your senses are unusually strong. You cannot be surprised by anything, and always have a chance to react first.

skills.name: Wind Runner
skills.rulesText: You can leap to anywhere you can see, run along walls, run as fast as a car, and, if you have an explanation, fly.

effect.text: You can leap to anywhere you can see, run along walls, run as fast as a car, and, if you have an explanation, fly.

actions.name: Damage
actions.rulesText: Deal 1 damage to an enemy within range. 3+: Deal 2 damage instead. 5+: Deal 3 damage instead, and Push 1. 7+: Deal 4 damage instead, and Push 2 instead. 9+: Deal 5 damage instead, and Push 3 instead.

actions.name: Throw
actions.rulesText: Push 1 to an adjacent enemy. 3+: Push 2 instead. 5+: Push 3 instead, and deal 1 damage to them. 7+: Push 4 instead, and deal 2 damage instead. 9+: Push 5 instead, and deal 3 damage instead.

actions.name: Grapple
actions.rulesText: Target someone within Range 1-X. Pull them 2. 4+: Pull 1 more and if they are an enemy, give them 1 Fatigue token. 7+: Pull 2 more and if they are an enemy, give them 2 Fatigue tokens.

actions.name: Stagger
actions.rulesText: Give 2 Fatigue tokens to an adjacent enemy. 7+: Give them 2 more Fatigue tokens and 2 Weakness tokens.

actions.name: A Challenger Approaches
actions.rulesText: Challenge an enemy within Range 1-4. 4+: Challenge up to two more enemies within Range 1-4.

actions.name: Put It Out!
actions.rulesText: Discard 1 non-Unique token from someone within range. 4+: Choose one: Discard 1 Unique token from them; -or-Discard up to 2 more non-Unique tokens from them. 7+: Choose one: Discard 1 Unique token from them; -or-Discard up to 2 more non-Unique tokens from them.

actions.name: Movement
actions.rulesText: You gain X Speed tokens.

actions.name: Open The Path
actions.rulesText: Target an obstacle within range and destroy it. 4+: Destroy up to 3 obstacles adjacent to the initial target. 8+: Destroy up to 5 obstacles within Range 1-3 of any previous target.

actions.name: Guard
actions.rulesText: You gain temporary Armor.

actions.name: Rescue
actions.rulesText: Choose one: Heal an ally within range; -or- heal an ally who is not in play, then return them to play into an empty space within range.

actions.name: Amplify
actions.rulesText: Your next Action this turn has its maximum range increased by 3, and may apply to one additional target.

actions.name: Shockwave
actions.rulesText: Unblockable by Armor and Shields. Deal 1 damage to each enemy within range. 6+: Deal 2 damage to one enemy within range.

actions.name: Suppression
actions.rulesText: You gain 1 Control token and may Move 1. 6+: You gain 1 Control token and may Move 1. 9+: You gain 1 Control token and may Move 1.

actions.name: Dance Together
actions.rulesText: Choose someone within range. Pull them 1, then you Move 1, then you Pull them 1 more. Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Tango
actions.rulesText: Swap spaces with an adjacent enemy, then Push them 1. 6+: Pull them 2, then deal 2 damage to them. 10+: Push them 4, then deal 3 damage to them.

actions.name: Dance Apart
actions.rulesText: Push 3 to someone within range, then Move 1. 7+: Move 2 more, then heal.

actions.name: Secure
actions.rulesText: Choose two: Gain 2 Iron tokens; -or- an ally within range other than yourself gains 2 Iron tokens; -or- give Shield 2 to an ally within range.

actions.name: Contain
actions.rulesText: Target an enemy within range, then Choose two: Challenge them; -or- Give them 2 Fatigue tokens; -or- place a Trap into their space.

actions.name: Protect
actions.rulesText: Choose four from the Secure and Contain lists. Options from the Contain list must target an enemy within range.

actions.name: Slide In
actions.rulesText: Teleport 2. 4+: Teleport 2 more, then you may deal 1 damage to an enemy within range.

actions.name: Left, Right!
actions.rulesText: Deal 1 damage to an enemy within range, then deal 2 damage to a different enemy within range.

actions.name: Yell
actions.rulesText: You gain Power tokens equal to half of X (rounded up), then you gain a Shield with a value equal to half of X (rounded down).

actions.name: Crush
actions.rulesText: Unblockable by Abilities and Tokens. Deal 3 damage to an enemy within range. 9+: Deal 5 damage instead, and Crush is Unblockable.

actions.name: Palm Strike
actions.rulesText: Push 3 and deal 1 damage to an adjacent enemy.

actions.name: Deep Breathing
actions.rulesText: Move up to 2. This movement ignores obstacles. At the start of the next turn, add X to your Action Pool. Usable once per turn. Unblockable.

actions.name: Rupture
actions.rulesText: An enemy within range gains X Burning Tokens. This can only target the active character.

actions.name: Stunt
actions.rulesText: Place one Fog, Copy, Pit, or Trap obstacle into an adjacent space, then teleport 2. During enemy turns: usable once per turn.

actions.name: Sing Along
actions.rulesText: Target an ally you can see. Choose one: They discard one token; -or- they heal 2; -or- they gain 2 tokens from your song. 4+: They also choose one from the list. 6+: Add a 4 to their Action Pool. Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Diss Track
actions.rulesText: Target an enemy you can see. Choose one to give them: 2 Burning tokens; -or- 2 Fatigue tokens; -or- 2 Weakness Tokens. 5+: They also choose one from the list. 6+: Pull 2 and Challenge them.

actions.name: Blossoms
actions.rulesText: You gain Shield 2 and choose one: Gain 1 Power token; -or- Move 1; -or- heal 1. 6+: Instead, gain Shield 4 and choose two.

actions.name: Brambles
actions.rulesText: This is a Token Action that costs your Shield. Deal 1 damage to up to X enemies within Range 1-X, then gain 1 Power token. X is equal to the value of the destroyed Shield. Usable twice per turn.

actions.name: Bow Down
actions.rulesText: Give 1 Weakness token to an enemy within range. 4+: Give 1 Weakness token to each enemy within range.

actions.name: Stand Strong
actions.rulesText: 1+: Give 1 Power token to an ally within range. 3+: Heal that ally. 5+: Heal and give 1 Power token to a different ally within range. Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Pounce
actions.rulesText: Pull yourself 3 towards an enemy you can see. Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Howl
actions.rulesText: Gain 1 Power token, then heal 4, then give 1 Weakness token to each enemy you can see. Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Purify
actions.rulesText: Discard one token from an ally within range. 3+: Discard up to two tokens from someone within range. 6+: Discard up to two tokens from someone within range.

actions.name: Denial
actions.rulesText: Teleport into an empty space adjacent to an enemy you can see, then Challenge them.

actions.name: Beacon
actions.rulesText: Pull up to 4 to an ally you can see, other than yourself. 4+, Once per turn: You and that ally heal.

actions.name: Blinding Light
actions.rulesText: Challenge an adjacent enemy, then Push 1 and give them 1 Burning token. 5+: Instead, Push 3 and give them 3 Burning tokens.

actions.name: Rip Chord
actions.rulesText: Give one of your Mood’s tokens to an enemy within Range. 5+: Give one of your Mood’s tokens to each enemy within Range. 8+: Give one of your Mood’s tokens to each enemy you can see.

actions.name: Mood Shift
actions.rulesText: Apply all of your Start Effects as this Action’s effects. Usable once per turn, only during your own turn.

actions.name: As The Crow Flies
actions.rulesText: Teleport 4. 4+: Challenge an enemy within range, then Teleport 2.

actions.name: Follow My Lead
actions.rulesText: You may move 1, then deal 1 damage to an enemy within range. An ally you can see (other than yourself) may move 1, then deal 1 damage to an enemy within their range. 6+: You may move 1, then deal 1 damage to an enemy within range. An ally you can see (other than yourself) may move 1, then deal 1 damage to an enemy within their range.

actions.name: Burning Heart
actions.rulesText: Each ally within range gains 2 Iron tokens and 2 Power tokens. Usable once per turn, only while you hold no Power tokens.

actions.name: Hero’s Moment
actions.rulesText: Deal 4 damage to an adjacent enemy and Push them X. X is equal to 2, or to half the damage on your current health bar, rounded up, whichever is higher.

actions.name: Leap In
actions.rulesText: Teleport 3. Then, deal 2 damage to an enemy within range.

actions.name: Leap Out
actions.rulesText: Deal 2 damage to an enemy within range, then teleport 3. Then, choose one: Deal 2 damage to a different enemy within range; -or-heal 2; -or-gain 2 Power tokens.

actions.name: Group Up
actions.rulesText: Pull up to 3 to one ally you can see. 3+: Pull up to 3 to one ally you can see. 5+, Once per turn: Choose one to apply to each ally within range: Heal; -or-Gain 2 Power tokens; -or-Gain Shield 3.

actions.name: Eyes Open
actions.rulesText: You gain 4 Iron Tokens and may Move 1.

actions.name: Stay Out Of This
actions.rulesText: Give 3 Weakness tokens and Push 3 to an enemy within range.

actions.name: Hard Body
actions.rulesText: You gain temporary Armor. 6+: You gain 4 Iron tokens.

actions.name: You, Stay
actions.rulesText: Challenge an enemy within range. Give that enemy 2 Fatigue tokens. 5 Iron: Instead give them 4 Fatigue tokens. You gain Shield 3. Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Overclock
actions.rulesText: Gain 2 Power tokens and 1 Burning token. 5+: Gain 2 more Power tokens and 1 more Burning token. Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Flamethrower
actions.rulesText: Deal 1 damage and give 1 Burning token to an enemy within range. 4 Power: Instead, deal 2 damage and give 2 Burning tokens, and also, Flamethrower now applies to each target adjacent to the initial target(s). Usable once per turn.

actions.name: High Efficiency
actions.rulesText: Choose two: You heal 1; -or-you gain 1 Iron token; -or-you gain 1 Power token; -or-you gain 1 Speed token; -or-you deal 1 damage to an enemy within range. 4+: Choose all five instead. 8+: Replace all 1’s in High Efficiency with 2’s.

actions.name: Nitro Boost
actions.rulesText: Teleport 2, then gain 2 Speed tokens. 6+: Teleport 2, then gain 3 Speed tokens.

actions.name: Rocket Tackle
actions.rulesText: Push 2 to someone within range. 5 Speed: If they are an ally, they Move up to 3. If they are an enemy, Push 2 and deal 2 damage to them. Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Power Converter
actions.rulesText: Target a single token held by you or someone within range. Choose one or both: You steal the targeted token(s) from them; and/or replace the targeted token(s) with Power tokens. 6+: Power Converter instead applies to every token they hold of the targeted token's type.

actions.name: Darkness Dawns
actions.rulesText: Place one or two Fog obstacles into empty spaces within range. You may teleport to an empty space within those Fog obstacles.

actions.name: Twilight Sorrow
actions.rulesText: Each enemy standing within Fog gains 1 Weakness token and 1 Fatigue token. Then, you gain 3 Speed tokens.

actions.name: Gate Guardian
actions.rulesText: Pull 2 to all enemies you can see, then deal 1 damage to each enemy within range.

actions.name: Watch Your Step
actions.rulesText: Target an enemy you can see that moved during this turn. You Push 1 and deal 2 damage to them.

actions.name: Suddenly…
actions.rulesText: Teleport into an empty space adjacent to someone who is alone, then if they are an enemy, you deal 1 damage to them. Someone is alone if nobody is adjacent to them.

actions.name: Life Steal
actions.rulesText: Deal 2 damage and give 1 Weakness token to an enemy within range.

actions.name: Hypnotic Gaze
actions.rulesText: Target an enemy you can see. Pull them up to 4, then if they are now within your range, give them 2 Weakness tokens.

actions.name: Hunger
actions.rulesText: One target within range discards 3 tokens of their choice (or all of their tokens, if they have less). For each token they discarded, place a Copy into an empty space adjacent to them.

actions.name: Raise The Dead
actions.rulesText: Give 2 Fatigue tokens to an enemy within range, then place 2 Copies in empty spaces adjacent to that enemy.

actions.name: Blazing Speed
actions.rulesText: Target an enemy you can see that has Burning Tokens. Pull yourself up to X spaces towards them, where X is the number of Burning Tokens they hold. Usable once per enemy turn.

actions.name: Ignition
actions.rulesText: Deal X damage to an adjacent enemy. X = the number of Burning tokens they hold. Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Demolition
actions.rulesText: Choose one: Place a Pit into a space within range; -or-place 2 Traps into spaces within range; -or-destroy up to 3 obstacles within range. 5+: Choose two instead. 7+: Choose three instead.

actions.name: Ka-Boom!
actions.rulesText: Place Rubble into an adjacent space, then destroy it. Push yourself 2 spaces away from that Rubble. 4+: Place Rubble into an adjacent space, then destroy it. Push yourself 2 or 3 spaces away from that Rubble. 6+: Place Rubble into an adjacent space, then destroy it. Push yourself up to 3 spaces away from that Rubble.

actions.name: Flame Guard
actions.rulesText: You can only use Flame Guard while you hold no Iron tokens. You gain 2 Iron tokens. Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Heat Beam
actions.rulesText: Unblockable. Deal 3 damage to an enemy you can see that is holding at least 2 Burning tokens, then they discard 2 Burning tokens.

actions.name: Cleansing Fire
actions.rulesText: Choose two: Give 2 Burning tokens to an enemy within range; -or- heal an ally within range; -or- discard up to 3 status tokens from an ally within range. Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Firebird’s Flight
actions.rulesText: Teleport 3, then give 2 Burning tokens to all adjacent enemies.

actions.name: Lava Walk
actions.rulesText: Move 1, then place a Trap into the space you left. Usable twice per turn.

actions.name: Pyroclasm
actions.rulesText: Place 3 Traps into spaces within range.

actions.name: Firing Wild
actions.rulesText: Choose one: Deal 1 damage to each adjacent enemy; -or- deal 1 damage to up to 3 enemies within range; -or- deal 1 damage to up to 2 enemies you can see beyond your maximum range. 5+: Choose two instead. 8+: Deal 2 damage instead.

actions.name: Kneecapper
actions.rulesText: This is a Gunslinger Action. Choose one or two enemies within range. Deal 1 damage and give 2 Fatigue tokens to each target.

actions.name: Take Aim
actions.rulesText: This is a Gunslinger Action. Your next damage-dealing Action is Unblockable by Armor, Iron Tokens, and Shields.

actions.name: Headshot
actions.rulesText: Deal 5 damage to an enemy within range. Usable once per Round.

actions.name: Bombardment
actions.rulesText: This is a Gunslinger Action. Place a Trap into any space within range. Then, deal 2 damage to each enemy adjacent to, or on, that Trap.

actions.name: Bazooka
actions.rulesText: Deal 4 damage to an enemy within range, then deal 1 damage and give 2 Burning tokens to an enemy adjacent to you.

actions.name: Point Blank Shot
actions.rulesText: Push 1 and deal 1 damage to an adjacent enemy. 4+: Instead, Push 3 and deal 3 damage.

actions.name: Showdown
actions.rulesText: This is a Gunslinger Action. Challenge an enemy within range. If they take the next turn for their side, they cannot discard your Challenge before the end of that turn. If they do not, you deal 3 damage to them. Usable once per turn. Unblockable by Shields.

actions.name: Trick Shot
actions.rulesText: Choose one obstacle within range. Destroy it, then deal 2 damage to an enemy within Range 1-3 of that obstacle. 6+: Then, deal 2 damage to an enemy within Range 1-3 of that first enemy. 9+: Then, deal 3 damage to a third enemy within Range 1-3 of that second enemy.

actions.name: Scatter Shot
actions.rulesText: This is a Gunslinger Action. Place Rubble into a space within range. Then, each enemy on or adjacent to that Rubble takes 1 damage and is pushed 3 spaces away from that Rubble.

actions.name: Aura Surge
actions.rulesText: Choose one: 1 ally within range gains Shield 3; -or-Remove up to 4 points of Shield from 1 enemy within range. If this breaks their Shield, deal 2 damage to them.

actions.name: Banshee's Wail
actions.rulesText: All enemies within range gain 1 Weakness token and take 2 damage. All Traps, Pits, and Walls within range become Rubble.

actions.name: Pull The Strings
actions.rulesText: Target an enemy or ally you can see. Pull them 3. 4+: Target an enemy or ally within range. Push them 3. 7+: Target an enemy or ally within range. Choose one: Push them up to 4; -or- Pull them up to 4.

actions.name: Now You See Me…
